title: [Henan University of Engineering X CLO] Provincial Transfer Principle
description: This chapter's course introduces you to the key points of dart manipulation, elimination, and slash-and-spread methods in garment structural design (draping/pattern making).

Hello everyone, today we are going to talk about sound transfer and cutting.  
This is a common processing method in women's makeup design.  
We divide it into three parts.  
The first part is about the principle of sound transfer and elimination.  
The second part is about the classification and design applications of sound transfer and elimination.  
The third part is about the classification and design applications of cutting.  

In the first part, we will discuss the principle of sound transfer and elimination.  
It mainly concerns the relationship between three-dimensional feeling and sound volume.  
We use the primitive form as an example.  
Let's say I want to form a cone shape like this.  
We all know that the cone shape is made up of a full circle and a fan shape.  
What about the missing corner of the fan shape?  
Suppose it is 90 degrees.  
No matter where I am within 90 degrees,  
whether it is on the left, on the right, or anywhere else,  
regardless of the location,  
the degree to which the cone shape is formed after sewing should be exactly the same as the first and second corners.  
Even if it is a 45-degree corner,  
or a 20-degree corner, or a 70-degree corner,  
the degree to which the cone shape is formed is exactly the same as the first two corners.  

Let's use the square shape as an example.  
The top shows a three-dimensional effect,  
and the bottom shows an open diagram of the four common cases.  
In other words,  
if I cut the square shape from anywhere,  
it will still be a completely identical shape after it is combined.  
The principle of sound transfer is the same as the principle of sound transfer.  

In the original form,  
our sounds are mainly chest sounds,  
dragon sounds,  
and so on.  
A, B, C, D, E, F sounds, and so on.  
In other words,  
the sound does not necessarily have to be in the original position.  
I can transfer it to any other position.  

Next, I will talk about the classification and design application of sound transfer and elimination.  
The name of the last sound and the method of sound transfer.  
Then, the design application:  
we will discuss the situation where we want to break the joint,  
and the situation where we do not want to break the joint.  

Next, let's first introduce the name and method of sound transfer of the last sound.  
Let's take the front as an example.  
Let's talk about the front first.  
The front is the name of the various sounds.  
We all know that the original sound,  
one is A,  
which is below B,  
and the other is B,  
which is below B.  
The C sound can be removed directly.  
Another very important one is the dragon sound.  

In fact, my sound does not necessarily have to be in the original position.  
If my sound is not in this position,  
and I set the sound to the neck,  
then it is called the neck sound.  
Set to the shoulder is called the shoulder sound.  
Set to the side is called the lower sound.  
Set to the front center line is called the front center sound.  
The waist is called the waist sound.  
This is the name of the structure line corresponding to which position it is in.  

The common ways of processing sound transfer are  
one, the straight cut method,  
and the other, the transfer method.  

The straight cut method,  
in the past,  
we needed to find a piece of paper,  
then remove the original shape,  
and then, for example, if I want to merge the B sound,  
we divide my original shape into the black part and the red part through the B sound.  
I need to cut off the red part,  
then paste it after adding it,  
and then paste the two sides of the sound together.  

In this way,  
I have completed the elimination of my B sound.  
If I want to change the position of a new sound,  
for example, I set the position of the new sound to the shoulder sound,  
I need to find a piece of paper,  
then remove the original shape,  
and then draw the position of the new sound.  
The position of the new sound is cut open with scissors,  
then merge the sound of the dragon sound,  
and then we draw the structure line smoothly.  
The red line is the final structure line.  
After drawing,  
I drag it onto my paper.  
This is the past of B sound.  
This is the whole process of practicing B sound.  

There is another method,  
which is the circular rotation method.  
I don't cut another piece of paper.  
I draw it on the circle.  

For example,  
the whole process of my work is still with the shoulder.  
Now we still use the shoulder as an example.  
Let's say that  
this is the circular rotation method.  
I want to draw a position of the new sound on the shoulder.  

After determining the position of the new sound,  
the position of the new sound and the sound of the dragon sound,  
I assume that the sound of A does not move.  
The position of the new sound and the sound of the dragon sound  
divide my original shape into the black part and the red part.  
I draw the black part first,  
then draw it on the paper.  
After that,  
I do not move according to the BP point.  
We merge the sound of the dragon sound,  
which is to rotate the red part,  
and rotate it accordingly.  
After that,  
I draw it again.  
Finally,  
I draw the position of the new sound.  

Of course,  
this process is very convenient  
if you have a CD later.  
However,  
if you are a beginner,  
you still need to have such training.  
This training is relatively  
easier to understand  
if you practice it.

we will explain in 3D  
how to rotate the sound.

chunks.content: # Provincial Transfer Principle *Henan University of Engineering X CLO* This document explains the principles, classification, and design applications of sound transfer and elimination, as well as cutting techniques used in women's makeup design, focusing on three-dimensional shape formation and structural line manipulation. --- ## Principles of Sound Transfer and Elimination This section covers the fundamental relationship between three-dimensional shape formation and sound volume, illustrating how shapes like cones and squares maintain their structure after cutting and recombining, which underpins the principle of sound transfer. - **Three-Dimensional Shape Example: Cone** - A cone shape is composed of a full circle and a fan shape with a missing corner (e.g., 90°, 45°, 20°, 70°). - Regardless of the angle of the missing corner or the position within it, the reconstructed cone maintains the same degree of shape formation after sewing. - **Square Shape Example** - A square's three-dimensional effect and open diagram demonstrate that cutting from any position results in an identical reconstructed shape. - This illustrates the principle that the shape's integrity is preserved regardless of the cutting position. - **Sound Transfer Concept** - In the original form, sounds correspond to specific structural lines or points (e.g., chest sounds, dragon sounds, A, B, C, D, E, F sounds). - Sounds do not need to remain in their original positions and can be transferred to different locations without altering the overall structure. --- ## Classification and Design Applications of Sound Transfer and Elimination This section details the terminology for different sound positions, methods for transferring sounds, and design considerations for breaking or maintaining joints. - **Terminology of Sound Positions** - Original sounds: - A sound (below B) - B sound (below B) - C sound (removable directly) - Dragon sound (important structural line) - Transferred sound names depend on new positions: - Neck sound (sound set to neck) - Shoulder sound - Lower sound (side) - Front center sound (front center line) - Waist sound - **Common Methods of Sound Transfer** 1. **Straight Cut Method** - Requires removing the original shape from paper. - Divide the original shape along the sound line into segments (e.g., black and red parts). - Cut off the segment to be eliminated or transferred (e.g., the red part). - Paste segments after adjustment to eliminate or reposition the sound. - Draw new structural lines smoothly and combine the pieces. - Example: Eliminating B sound or transferring sound to the shoulder sound position. 2. **Circular Rotation Method** - No additional paper is needed; the shape is drawn on a circle. - After positioning the new sound, divide the shape into parts (black and red). - Draw and fix the black part. - Rotate the red part around a fixed point (e.g., BP point) to merge sounds (such as the dragon sound). - Draw the final structure line after rotation and merging. - This method is efficient and convenient, especially with a CD tool, but beginners benefit from hands-on practice.

Detailed explanation and demonstration of this process are intended to follow for practical training. --- # Summary - **Sound transfer and elimination** are techniques that manipulate structural lines ("sounds") in three-dimensional design to preserve or alter shape volume and form. - Shapes like cones and squares demonstrate that cutting and rejoining along sound lines maintain consistent three-dimensional effects. - **Sound positions** have specific names depending on their location (neck, shoulder, waist, etc.). - Two primary methods for sound transfer exist: **Straight Cut** and **Circular Rotation**, each with procedural steps for cutting, rotating, and merging parts of the shape. - Understanding and practicing these methods, including the 3D rotation of sounds, are essential for mastering design applications in makeup and related fields.
